summary: The change lowers anonymous object literals into canonical, content-addressed shape classes (sorted field identity, shared across property orders and readonly/optional views), routes record-like literals to maps, picks union constituents via checker assignability, and preserves JS evaluation order via temps; empty literals use contextual shapes. The full test suite plus adversarial probes (nesting, spreads, conditionals/closures/switch, initializers, records, cross-file shape sharing, readonly/writable view mixing) all verify, emit through ABAP, and run correctly through the Go backend, and the patch also fixes latent baseline bugs (same-key union misselection causing 'string <- i32', a leaked l.hint, and a nil-ctor panic path). Remaining nits are minor and pre-existing.

findings.claim: The evaluation-order fix is gated on the 'shape.' name prefix, so an anonymous literal that reuses a named alias shape class (the shapeLike reuse path in synthFromProperties, lower_types.go:609) still evaluates property initializers in constructor/declaration order instead of source order. Equivalent literals therefore get different evaluation semantics depending on whether a named alias shape happened to be synthesized first. Pre-existing for named aliases (baseline reproduces it too), not a regression, but the fix is incomplete/asymmetric for the feature area this change touches.
findings.repro: Probe test (tsfront): type Row = {name: string; count: number}; export function use(r: Row): number { return r.count; } export class Probe { static counter: number = 0; static next(): number {this.counter += 1; return this.counter;} static run(): number { use({count: 5, name: "x"}); const v = {count: this.next(), name: "name" + this.next()}; return v.count * 10 + this.counter; } } -> runGoHIR prints "22"; JavaScript semantics give v.count=1, counter=2 => "12". Same wrong result on baseline, so pre-existing.

findings.claim: In the shape-reuse paths (lines 642 and 696), the Readonly update only mutates a copy stored in l.fields; the reused hir.Class.Fields entry is never updated, so a shared shape's Readonly flags reflect whichever view was synthesized first, and the flag written into l.fields is not consumed by any pass (only class Fields feed number_ranges/golang classify). Inert/misleading metadata rather than a miscompile.
